name: Ravenswood Business District / 4 Corners Specific Plan
acresNote: The adopted Specific Plan (p. 4 of the plan, PDF p. 13) says the Plan Area encompasses approximately 207 acres; the December 2024 notices of determination also give 207 acres. The plan area excludes University Village, the single-family neighborhood it wraps around. The 2022 notice of preparation gave 350 acres, and the City's GIS 'Specific Plan Boundary' polygon measures about 326 acres because it takes in University Village. It is a plan area of many properties, not one site.

program.notes: Net new development the plan allows (Table 4-1, Growth Scenario 2): 3,350,000 sq ft of office and R&D, 300,000 sq ft of industrial, 112,400 sq ft of retail, 154,700 sq ft of community and civic space, 53,500 sq ft of tenant amenity space and 1,600 homes (1,472 multifamily, 128 single-family or townhouse). Office/R&D space is handed out by City Council allocation: 2,700,000 sq ft for standard projects, a 250,000 sq ft reserve for projects under 150,000 sq ft and a 400,000 sq ft reserve for 'exemplary' projects. The City's inclusionary ordinance requires 20% of new homes to be affordable on site, or an alternative. The environmental notices give 3.3 million sq ft of office/R&D and 129,700 sq ft of civic space; the adopted plan's table is used here. Tallest buildings (seven to eight stories) go at the east end of Bay Road, at Four Corners and in the employment core.

stageNote: The City Council certified the environmental review and amended the General Plan on Dec 3, 2024, and adopted the updated specific plan and zoning on second reading on Dec 17, 2024, replacing the 2013 plan. Each project still needs its own approval; no office/R&D allocation under the 2024 plan has been found in City Council agendas through October 2026. The largest proposal in the area, Emerson Collective's East Palo Alto Waterfront, has a 299-home first phase under review.

timeline.event: City adopts the original Ravenswood/4 Corners TOD Specific Plan.
City Council starts the plan update to study a larger buildout.
The City issues the notice of preparation for a subsequent EIR (SCH 2022040352).
The City releases the Draft Subsequent EIR.
The City releases the Final Subsequent EIR.
Design review application filed for East Palo Alto Waterfront Phase 1 (299 homes, about 11,000 sq ft of community and commercial space).
City Council certifies the Final SEIR, amends the General Plan and introduces the specific plan and zoning ordinances (4 ayes, 1 abstention).
City Council adopts the updated Ravenswood Business District/4 Corners Specific Plan and zoning amendments on second reading.

City Council hears the appeal of the 1675 Bay Road (Four Corners) townhome and mixed-use projects, 274 homes in all, which the Planning Commission had declined to approve; the City now lists both as approved.

summary: A rezoning of East Palo Alto's Ravenswood Business District and Four Corners, between University Village and the Bay, to allow up to 3.35 million sq ft of new office and R&D space and 1,600 homes. It's a zoning plan rather than a single development: each property owner builds under it with its own approvals.
